patient.name: Name
patient.caseTitle: Example 1 — Acute Decompensated HFrEF With Pneumonia and Acute Kidney Injury

intro: This plan is based on the attached discharge example for a 72-year-old man with heart failure EF 30%, pneumonia, and improved acute kidney injury. Use it to review medications, follow-up steps, and daily care guidance before your next appointment.

checkIn.description: Record each scheduled dose separately, plus daily weight and symptoms. Follow your discharge instructions; meal timing is not specified.

medications.label: Metformin 500 mg · only continue if your care team confirms your kidneys are working well enough for this medicine

symptoms: New or worsening shortness of breath, especially at rest
Rapidly worsening leg or abdominal swelling
Fever or worsening cough despite antibiotics
warningSigns.summary: Seek urgent medical attention for new or worsening shortness of breath (especially at rest), chest pain or pressure, fainting or severe dizziness, rapidly worsening leg or abdominal swelling, significantly reduced urine output, new confusion or severe weakness, or fever/worsening cough despite antibiotics.
warningSigns.emergency: Severe symptoms or immediate danger — call your local emergency number; do not wait for chat.
warningSigns.emergencyShort: Severe symptoms or immediate danger: call your local emergency number.
warningSigns.contactTeam: Contact your heart-failure team promptly for rapid weight gain or worsening swelling/breathlessness, following your individualized discharge plan.

list.name: Losartan
list.purpose: For heart failure and blood pressure.

list.name: Metformin
list.note: Only continue if your care team confirms your kidneys are working well enough to keep taking it.

stopped.title: Stopped / held / avoid
items: Spironolactone — held pending repeat renal function and potassium.
Ibuprofen/other NSAIDs — avoid due to heart failure and recent kidney injury unless specifically approved by your treating clinician.

teaching.title: Nursing teaching
items: Furosemide increases urination; discuss earlier-in-day timing when possible. This is teaching guidance, not an additional dosing instruction.
Apixaban: review bleeding precautions and notify clinicians about new medications.

tasks.title: Arrange a basic metabolic panel
tasks.detail: Before or at early outpatient follow-up to reassess creatinine and potassium.

tasks.title: Arrange primary-care follow-up
tasks.detail: Within approximately 1 week of discharge. Scheduling status not provided.

tasks.title: Arrange cardiology follow-up
tasks.detail: Within approximately 1 week of discharge. Scheduling status not provided.

dailyCare: Weigh yourself at approximately the same time each morning; record weight and symptoms.
Low-sodium diet: approximately 2 grams of sodium daily.
Follow fluid recommendations from your heart-failure team; no numeric fluid limit is supplied.
Finish the entire antibiotic course even if feeling better.

items.title: Primary-care follow-up
details: Within approximately 1 week of discharge. No discharge date or booked appointment is supplied.
Basic metabolic panel before or at early follow-up: creatinine and potassium.

items.title: Cardiology follow-up
details: Within approximately 1 week of discharge. Scheduling status not provided.
Confirm follow-up appointments and laboratory testing with your care team.

appointments.note: Contact your heart-failure team promptly for rapid weight gain or worsening swelling/breathlessness, following your individualized discharge plan. No numeric weight-gain threshold is supplied.
